```{r, echo = FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning=FALSE)
# plotly.js from the CDN, so the site's pages don't each copy it
options(plotly.core.plotlyjs = "cdn")
```

A [Choropleth Map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choropleth_map) is a map composed of colored polygons. It is used to represent spatial variations of a quantity. This page documents how to build **tile-map** choropleth maps, but you can also build [**outline** choropleth maps using the `choropleth` trace type](choropleth-maps.html).

Below we show how to create Choropleth Maps using the plotly.core `add_choroplethmap()` trace (see `go_choroplethmap()`).

### Base Map Configuration

plotly.core bundles plotly.js 4, where the Mapbox-based `choroplethmapbox` trace was replaced by the MapLibre-based `choroplethmap` trace. Base map styles such as `"carto-positron"` and `"open-street-map"` need no access token. See our [Map Layers](mapbox-layers.html) documentation for more information.

### Introduction: main parameters for choropleth tile maps

Making choropleth tile maps requires two main types of input:

1. GeoJSON-formatted geometry information where each feature has either an `id` field or some identifying value in `properties`.
2. A list of values indexed by feature identifier.

The GeoJSON data is passed to the `geojson` argument, and the data is passed into the `z` argument of `add_choroplethmap()`.

**Note** the `geojson` attribute can also be the URL to a GeoJSON file, which can speed up map rendering in certain cases.

#### GeoJSON with `feature.id`

Here we load a GeoJSON file containing the geometry information for US counties, where `feature.id` is a [FIPS code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIPS_county_code).

```{r}
library(jsonlite)
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/geojson-counties-fips.json"
json_file <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
json_file$features[[1]]$id
```

### Data indexed by `id`

Here we load unemployment data by county, also indexed by [FIPS code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIPS_county_code).

```{r}
df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/fips-unemp-16.csv", header = T, colClasses = c("fips" = "character"))
head(df)
```
### Tile Map Choropleth Map Using GeoJSON

With `choroplethmap`, each row of the data frame is represented as a region of the choropleth.

```{r}
library(jsonlite)
library(plotly.core)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/geojson-counties-fips.json"
counties <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
url2 <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/fips-unemp-16.csv"
df <- read.csv(url2, colClasses = c(fips = "character"))
fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_choroplethmap(
    geojson = counties,
    locations = df$fips,
    z = df$unemp,
    colorscale = "Viridis",
    zmin = 0,
    zmax = 12,
    marker = go_choroplethmap_marker(
      line = go_choroplethmap_marker_line(width = 0),
      opacity = 0.5
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "carto-positron",
      zoom = 2,
      center = go_map_center(lon = -95.71, lat = 37.09)
    )
  )
fig
```

### Tile Map Choropleth Map Using GeoJSON with `featureidkey`
If the GeoJSON you are using either does not have an `id` field or you wish you use one of the keys in the `properties` field, you may use the `featureidkey` parameter to specify where to match the values of locations.

In the following GeoJSON object/data-file pairing, the values of `properties.district` match the values of the `district` column:
```{r}
library(plotly.core)
library(jsonlite)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/election.geojson"
geojson <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
url2 <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/election.csv"
df <- read.csv(url2)
fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_choroplethmap(
    geojson = geojson,
    locations = df$district,
    z = df$Bergeron,
    colorscale = "Viridis",
    featureidkey = "properties.district",
    colorbar = go_colorbar(title = "Bergeron Votes")
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "carto-positron",
      zoom = 9,
      center = go_map_center(lon = -73.7073, lat = 45.5517)
    )
  )
fig
```

#### Carto Voyager base map: no token needed

```{r}
library(jsonlite)
library(plotly.core)

url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/geojson-counties-fips.json"
counties <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
url2 <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/fips-unemp-16.csv"
df <- read.csv(url2, colClasses = c(fips = "character"))

fig <- go_figure() |>
  add_choroplethmap(
    geojson = counties,
    locations = df$fips,
    z = df$unemp,
    colorscale = "Viridis",
    zmin = 0,
    zmax = 12,
    marker = go_choroplethmap_marker(
      line = go_choroplethmap_marker_line(width = 0),
      opacity = 0.5
    )
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    map = go_map(
      style = "carto-voyager",
      zoom = 3,
      center = go_map_center(lon = -95.7129, lat = 37.0902)
    )
  )
fig
```

See `go_choroplethmap()` for more information and options!
